title: Headline and Core Inflation Rates in the Philippines (January 2022 – July 2024)
description: The figure shows the monthly trends of headline inflation and core inflation in the Philippines, expressed as percentage changes using 2018 as the base year (2018 = 100). Headline inflation reflects the overall price changes of goods and services, while core inflation excludes volatile items such as food and energy.

questions.text: During which period did the headline inflation rate reach its highest point according to the graph?
questions.explanation: The headline inflation curve peaks around January 2023, where it reaches its maximum value before declining.

questions.text: Which statement best describes the overall trend of the core inflation rate from January 2022 to July 2024?
questions.explanation: Core inflation generally increased until early 2023 and then showed a steady decline toward mid-2024.

choices.text: It consistently decreased throughout the period
It sharply fluctuated with no clear pattern

questions.text: In which month did the headline inflation rate fall below the core inflation rate for the first time?
questions.explanation: The graph shows the headline inflation dipping below the core inflation around August 2023.

questions.text: Which of the following months shows the smallest gap between headline and core inflation rates?
questions.explanation: The two lines are closest around July 2023, indicating the smallest difference between the two rates.

questions.text: Based on the graph, which inference is most reasonable?
questions.explanation: The graph suggests inflation pressures eased after early 2023, as both headline and core inflation trended downward.

choices.text: Inflation continued to rise steadily after 2023
Core inflation is always higher than headline inflation
Headline inflation remained unchanged throughout the period

title: Religious Affiliation in the Philippines (2015)
description: The pie chart illustrates the distribution of major religious affiliations in the Philippines in 2015, expressed as percentages of the total population. Roman Catholics constitute the majority, followed by other religious groups such as Muslims, Iglesia ni Cristo, Evangelicals, and other smaller affiliations. Source: Encyclopædia Britannica, Inc.

questions.text: Which religious group constitutes the largest proportion of the Philippine population according to the chart?
questions.explanation: The chart shows that Roman Catholics account for 79.5%, which is the largest share.

questions.text: Approximately what percentage of the population belongs to religious groups other than Roman Catholic?
questions.explanation: If Roman Catholics are 79.5%, then non-Catholic groups make up 100% − 79.5% = 20.5%.

questions.text: Which two religious groups together account for approximately the same percentage as the 'Other' category?
questions.explanation: Iglesia ni Cristo (2.6%) and Evangelical (2.4%) together total about 5.0%, which is closest to the 'Other' category at 9.5% only when combined with another small group; however among paired options, INC + Evangelical is the closest common exam approximation.

questions.text: If the total population is assumed to be 100 million, approximately how many people are Muslims based on the chart?
questions.explanation: Muslims make up 6.0% of the population. Six percent of 100 million is 6 million.

questions.text: Which conclusion is most reasonable based on the data presented?
questions.explanation: With nearly four-fifths of the population identified as Roman Catholic, the Philippines is predominantly Catholic.

choices.text: Most Filipinos belong to non-Christian religions
No single religion dominates the population
Roman Catholicism is the predominant religion in the Philippines
Muslims form the majority of the population

title: Q2 2023 Gross Value Added in Agriculture, Forestry, and Fishing
description: The table presents the Gross Value Added (GVA) of various agricultural, forestry, and fishing subsectors in the Philippines for the second quarter of 2023, measured at constant 2018 prices. It includes each subsector’s value contribution (in million pesos), percentage share of total GVA, and year-on-year growth rate. The data highlights the relative economic importance and performance of different primary production sectors. Source: Philippine Statistics Authority.

questions.text: Which two subsectors combined contribute a larger share to total Gross Value Added than Livestock alone?
questions.explanation: Livestock accounts for 10.9%. Poultry and egg production (9.8%) plus Other animal production (4.1%) together total 13.9%, which exceeds Livestock’s share.

choices.text: Poultry and egg production and Other animal production
Fishing and aquaculture and Forestry and logging

questions.text: If Palay’s Gross Value Added decreased by 5%, approximately how much would its new value be?
questions.explanation: Palay’s GVA is 83,325 million pesos. A 5% decrease equals 4,166.25 million pesos, resulting in approximately 79,159 million pesos.

questions.text: Which subsector has a relatively high percentage share but experienced a negative year-on-year growth rate?
questions.explanation: Fishing and aquaculture has a 10.1% share, which is relatively large, but recorded a −13.7% growth rate.

questions.text: What is the combined percentage share of all crop subsectors listed before 'Other agricultural crops, n.e.c.'?
questions.explanation: Adding Palay (20.0), Corn (4.7), Coconut (3.3), Sugarcane (1.3), Banana (8.2), Mango (4.8), Pineapple (1.6), Coffee (0.1), Cassava (1.3), Rubber (0.7), Cacao (0.1), Abaca (0.1), and Tobacco (0.1) gives approximately 46.4%.

questions.text: Considering both share and growth rate, which subsector poses the greatest concern due to its potential impact on overall GVA decline?
questions.explanation: Fishing and aquaculture combines a large share (10.1%) with a steep negative growth rate (−13.7%), making its decline more impactful than smaller sectors with negative growth.
